en: The Three Powers of the Nestorian Teaching grant deliverance;
the supreme heavens offer profound reverence and praise. The great earth deeply contemplates universal peace;
the human source of true nature relies upon them for refuge. The compassionate father of the three realms is the Arhat.
All virtuous multitudes pay homage with utmost sincerity; All those of wise nature sing praises in song.
All who possess the truth look up to you in reverence; Receiving the compassionate light of the Sage, they are saved from demonic calamities.
Seeking nothing less than the True and Constant, The Compassionate Father, the Enlightened Son, the Pure Wind King.
Among all emperors, he is the Emperor of Teachers; among all World-Honored Ones, he is the Dharma Sovereign.
He eternally dwells in the wondrously luminous realm without boundaries. His radiant majesty thoroughly examines the frontiers of the realms of existence;
from the beginning, no person has ever been able to see him, nor can he be seen through physical form, for he possesses no marks.
Only you possess peerless, serene, and pure virtue; Only you possess divine majesty and incomparable power.
Only you remain unchanging and solemnly present; The root of all goodness, moreover, is infinite.
I now contemplate all your compassionate grace, Praising that wondrous bliss which illuminates this land.
Mishaha, Universal Honored One, Great Sage’s Son, Who extensively delivers the realms of suffering and saves countless beings;

King of Eternal Life, compassionate and joyful as a lamb, Greatly and universally immersed in the suffering of others without wearying, You vow to relinquish the heavy accumulated sins of all sentient beings; May you well protect our true nature, for which there is no other way.
The Noble Son sits upright at his father’s right side; His seat is further transcendent, vast, and high.
O Great Teacher, we pray that you accept this assembly’s invitation; Please descend upon the raft so that we may avoid drifting in the river of fire.
The Great Teacher is our compassionate father; The Great Teacher is our noble sovereign.
The Great Master is our Dharma King; the Great Master is able to provide universal salvation.
The Great Master’s power of wisdom assists all beings; all eyes gaze upon him without a moment’s wavering.
Furthermore, he bestows nectar upon the withered and parched, so that all who receive this moisture may cause their roots of goodness to flourish.
Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, I praise the Compassionate Father, the Ocean-Treasury of Compassion, the Great Sage of Humility and the Nature of Pure Wind.
The translucent Dharma-ear, the inconceivable realized body, Lokanātha Kusuma. The three bodies above are unified as one essence.
King Yuhanan, King Luga, and King Mojueci.
The Dharma Kings Mingtai, Mushi, and Duohui.
Jing Tong Dharma King,
Bao Lu Dharma King,
Qian Yan Dharma King.
The Dharma King Nanyiyi,
the Dharma King Minyan,
and the Dharma King Masajisi.
The Dharma King Yehuzi, the Dharma King Momeizi,
and the Dharma King Cenwen Seng.
The twenty-four holy Dharma Kings:
Khānāya Dharmarāja, Hasāya Dharmarāja, and so forth.
Misha-ye Dharma-rāja, Sa-ra Dharma-rāja,
and Ku-lu Dharma-rāja.
In response to the Dharma King’s message, I respectfully pay homage to the *Sūtra of the Constantly Radiant Imperial Music*,
the *Sūtra of the Supreme Ultimate Reaching the Source*,
and the *Sūtra of the Profound Will for Peaceful Bliss*.
The *Tian bao zang jing* (Sūtra of the Celestial Treasure Treasury), the *Duohui shengwang jing* (Sūtra of King Duohui),
and the *Asiguli yong jing* (Sūtra of Asiguli).
The Scripture of the Mysterious Origin, the Scripture of Penetrating Truth, and the Scripture of Precious Radiance.
*Chuanhuajing*, *Qingyijing*, *Yuanyijing*,
and *Lingjing*.
A Brief Exposition of the Sūtra on the Three Time Periods and the Sūtra on Interrogation and Examination.
One should contemplate the Sūtra that Proclaims the Meaning,
the Sūtra of the Ocean of the Master’s Benefits.
The Sūtra of the Dharma King Ratnamārga,
the Sūtra of the Vinaya of the Deleted River,
and the Sūtra of the Moon-Thought of Artistry.
The *Ningyeyu jing* (Scripture on the Auspiciousness of the World), the *Yize lüjing* (Scripture on the Vinaya of Ritual Rules), and the *Piyueqi jing* (Scripture on the Arising of the Vows).
The Sūtra of the Threefold Majestic Praise, the Sūtra of King Mūṣa,
and the Sūtra of Ilīya.
The Sūtra of the Suppression of Forests;
The Sūtra on Reporting News to the Dharma King;
The Sūtra of Miśika’s Sovereignty over Heaven and Earth.
The Scripture of the Four Gates,
the Scripture of the Opening of Truth, and the Scripture of Masajis.
The *Maitrībalasūtra* and the *Uśanasūtra*:
I have carefully examined the catalogs of various scriptures and find that the total number of sūtras translated during the Qin dynasty amounts to five hundred and thirty sections.
These were all written on palm leaves in the Sanskrit language.
In the ninth year of the Zhenguan era of Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty,
the great virtuous monk from the Western Regions, Amoghavajra (A-lo-ben), arrived in the Central Kingdom.
The original text was then performed together with its musical accompaniment.
Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng proclaimed and translated it for the audience.
Later, the great virtuous monk Jingjing of the original school was summoned.
The thirty sections and scrolls mentioned above have already been translated;
the remainder, numbering in great quantity, remain complete within the palm-leaf caskets and have not yet been translated.
